# Notifications — Vars

Var definitions are derived from `module.lowdefy.yaml`. Pass these via the `vars:` block in your app's `lowdefy.yaml` entry for this module.

## Summary

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `send_routine` | array | `[]` |  | API routine steps that shape app events into notification items and dispatch them (typically ending in a CallApi to dispatch-notifications). Receives event_ids in the payload. Default is an empty routine (no-op).  |
| `popup_limit` | number | `3` |  | Maximum number of popup notification toasts shown at once. The layout page component fetches this many unread notifications flagged popup:true and renders them as a fixed-position toast stack.  |
| `views` | array | `[]` |  | Inbox views: named groups of notification types shown at the top of the inbox rail, such as Mentions. Each view filters the inbox to its types, and its count is the sum of their unread counts. A record's type is its `type` (the notification id), else a legacy record's `event_type`.  |
| `sounds` | array | `[]` |  | Notification sounds the viewer can pick from, for the page-wide player (the `notification-sound` export) and the inbox's Sound switch. The first is the default, and a pick no longer listed falls back to it. A sound without `src` is the synthesised chirp. Empty plays the chirp. Pass the same list to a NotificationSound block with `picker: true` to let the viewer pick.  |
| `live` | boolean | `true` |  | Live notifications: the bell, the toast stack and the inbox update the moment a notification arrives or is read elsewhere, through a change stream per signed-in user with a page open. Needs MongoDB as a replica set (Atlas is one) and a host that serves websockets (on Vercel, turn on Fluid Compute for the project). Set false where change streams or websockets cannot run; the bell and toasts then update on navigation.  |
| `server_url` | string |  |  | Absolute origin used to compose email link URLs (e.g. https://app.example.com). Defaults to the url of the current Lowdefy environment (config.environments), so an app that declares its environments leaves it unset. Required otherwise when notification items carry page links.  |
| `public_link_types` | array | `["invite-user","resend-user-invite","user-invite"]` |  | Notification type values whose landing links resolve without a session (pre-auth flows such as user invites). Matched against both the legacy event_type field and the pipeline's type field.  |
| `filter_exempt_types` | array | `["invite-user","resend-user-invite","user-invite"]` |  | Notification type values exempt from the email recipient filter (email.filter / sendgrid.filter) — mail for these types always delivers to the actual recipient. Defaults to the pre-auth invite flows (the same set as public_link_types), which are useless when redirected. Set to an empty list to filter every type.  |
| `transport` | string | `smtp` |  | Email transport for the dispatch pipeline. "smtp" (default) sends SMTPMailSend over the notifications-email connection; "sendgrid" sends SendGridMailSend over the notifications-email-sendgrid connection (SendGrid HTTP API). Any other value throws on dispatch.  |
| `email` |  |  |  | SMTP transport for notification emails, used when transport is "smtp" (the default). Ignored when the app remaps the notifications-email connection to its own email connection.  |
| `sendgrid` |  |  |  | SendGrid HTTP API transport for notification emails, used when transport is "sendgrid". Ignored when the app remaps the notifications-email-sendgrid connection to its own connection.  |
